# FreshSave: Simulated Single-Store Fresh Food Waste Dataset

**This dataset is SIMULATED.** It was generated by the script `make_store_dataset.py` (included). It is not data from a real supermarket.
Product types, shelf lives, demand levels and prices use typical retail values; the simulated rules are written in the script.

## What one row is
One batch of fresh food on one evening of its shelf life (a daily snapshot). The question each row answers: **will this batch end with 20% or more of its units wasted?**

## Size
- 25,555 rows, 13 columns, no missing values
- 5,976 batches, 1 store, 8 categories, 49 product types (sub-categories)
- About 43% of batches are at risk

## Columns
| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| batch_id | Identifier of the delivered batch. Rows with the same batch_id are the same batch on different evenings |
| category | Fresh-food category (Bakery, Beverages, Dairy, Deli, Meat, Produce, Ready_to_Eat, Seafood) |
| sub_category | Product type, for example Whole Milk, Greek Yogurt, Salmon Fillet, Croissants |
| shelf_life_days | Total shelf life of the batch when it arrived |
| days_left | Days left to sell on this evening (the expiry evening itself is not a row, so it is 1 or more) |
| units_received | Units delivered in the batch |
| units_left | Units still on the shelf at the end of this evening |
| avg_daily_demand | The product's normal units sold per day |
| units_sold_today | Units sold on this day |
| cost_price | Cost per unit |
| handling_score | How well the batch was stored and moved, 1 (poor) to 10 (excellent) |
| is_promoted | 1 if the batch was on promotion, else 0 |
| **at_risk** | **Target.** 1 if 20% or more of the batch was wasted at the end of its life, else 0. The same value on every row of a batch |

## Split
Rows are in time order (earlier batches first).
- `store_train_70.csv`: first 17,888 rows (70.0%), 4,195 batches, at risk 41.9% of rows
- `store_test_30.csv`: last 7,667 rows (30.0%), 1,781 batches, at risk 40.4% of rows
- `store_data_25555.csv`: all rows together
No batch appears in both files. If you split the data yourself, split by `batch_id` in time order, **not at random rows**, otherwise the same batch leaks into training and testing and scores look too good.

## How the data was simulated (summary)
Each product is delivered every few days. The manager orders about normal demand x shelf life, with ordering error. Each batch has its own demand level, unknown on delivery day. Daily sales follow normal demand, the batch's demand level, a weekday effect (weekends sell more), a freshness effect (sales slow near expiry) and random noise. Poor handling spoils a small share of the stock each day. Whatever is left at the end of the shelf life is waste. The share of at-risk batches was calibrated to about 42%.

## Suggested uses
Classification (will a batch be wasted?), model comparison (KNN, Decision Tree and others), practising feature engineering, for example `units_received - units_left` (sold so far) and `units_left / avg_daily_demand - days_left` (stock cover versus days left).

## Limits
- Simulated data: scores on it show a method works, not how it would perform in a real store.
- One store only.
